answer: PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) is the automotive industry's standard supplier-qualification method — specified by AIAG — that a supplier uses to prove that a mass-production part, the process that makes it, and the plant's capability all meet the customer's design requirements before series production starts. It typically consists of submitting a package of evidence (dimensional and material test results, functional test results, process capability studies, and a Part Approval Process Checklist) to the customer for review and sign-off, with several element types and submission levels varying by customer and part. If you'd like, I can look up our own or a specific customer's PPAP requirements and submission level from the company records for this automotive category.
